facts.condition: For a finite mesh of posterior biases containing zero, one-half, and one, any receiver with a two-symbol source alphabet and finitely many observations admits a representation using no more observations than mesh sites while preserving every mesh-indexed information value; a reflection-compatible mesh also preserves paired symmetry.

On the three-site mesh, the auxiliary receiver optimization has the entropy-defined constant specified by the accepted claim as its infimum both for arbitrary finite receiver pairs and for reflection-paired receivers.

If the converse functional is bounded at or above that constant but strictly below twice it, each receiver's midpoint statistic must lie in the explicit interval derived by the accepted claim; this restriction is necessary rather than sufficient.

assumptions: All converse quantities, receiver statistics, and reflection operations use the definitions fixed in the builder-owned target state.
The finite-mesh conclusions are not extended to unrestricted posterior supports without an additional argument.
The three-site extremum is treated only as an auxiliary converse ingredient, not as a terminal sum-capacity result.
